Vector indexes require signiﬁcant compute resources to build data structures such as Hierarchical
Navigable Small Worlds (HNSW) graphs. When you enable GPU-acceleration on your domain or
collection, OpenSearch automatically detects opportunities to accelerate your index builds and
oﬄoads the index builds to GPU instances. OpenSearch Service manages the GPU instances on
your behalf, assigning them to your domain or collection when needed. This means you don't
manage utilization or pay for idle time.
You pay only for useful processing through Compute Units (OCU) - Vector Acceleration. Each Vector
Acceleration OCU is a combination of approximately 8 GiB of CPU memory, 2 vCPUs, and 6 GiB of
GPU memory. For more information, see the section called “ GPU Acceleration Pricing”.
To enable GPU acceleration for your domain or collection, see Enabling GPU-acceleration.
